subject: Re: Follow-up: model-fit & prompt collection — Acme discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Model-fit follow-up & prompt collection — next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good to meet the Acme team. Quick recap + proposed next steps to keep momentum on model fit and the evals we discussed.

Recap (short):
- Primary use case: product help desk summarization + triage + follow-up suggestion.
- Volume: ~3M monthly short-text tickets, median length ~120 tokens, 95th pct < 600 tokens.
- Key constraints: low-latency sub-300ms tail for quick answers, strong precision on instruction-following to avoid hallucinations.

Recommended next steps:
1) Prompt set collection: please share ~100 representative prompts across categories (summaries, classification, follow-ups, edge-cases). See attached template (prompt_collection_template.csv) for format. If possible include: original user text, desired output, category tag, and examples of edge-case failures you worry about.
2) Redaction guidance: if prompts include PII or PHI, either upload to our secure S3 share (I can send a link) or provide a redacted version + a small sample of raw examples. Don’t send full production dumps without the S3 link.
3) Initial model fit eval: we'll run the prompt set across 2 candidate configs and return quality metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency, cost). My initial recommendation: redwood-13b-quant (best cost/quality balance) and redwood-3-small (low-latency fallback).
4) Timing: if you can share the prompt CSV by EOD Fri (6/26), we can return a first-pass report by Tue (6/30).

Benchmarks / references: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-model-fit-2026 (we’ll upload the initial run there)

Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv (CSV)

Questions for you:
- Will the prompt examples include raw user PII? If yes, do you prefer us to request a secure upload link or do you want to send redacted copies?
- Any additional edge-cases (e.g., multilingual, legal language) we should prioritize?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min sync if easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit follow-up & prompt collection — next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a first pass: acme_initial_prompts.csv (includes ~60 representative prompts across the main product types). 

Quick answers to your Qs:
- Yes, some prompts will contain customer PII (emails, support ticket IDs). We can't share raw production dumps in email. A secure upload link would be ideal.
- Multilingual: a small slice (~5%) of tickets are Spanish; we flagged them in the CSV.
- Edge-cases: we care a lot about 1) references to internal ticket IDs that should not be exposed, 2) very short context (<20 chars), and 3) tickets that include code snippets.

Example rows (from attached file):
1) "User: My app crashed after update. Error: NullPointer at line 157" -> desired: "Short summary + suggested triage steps" (category: crash-summary)
2) "How do I reset my billing?" -> desired: "Step-by-step billing reset instructions" (category: howto)
3) "Necesito reiniciar mi app" -> desired: "Spanish short summary + steps" (category: multilingual)

We can upload the raw data to the secure share — please send the link and I’ll coordinate with our security team.

Attachment: acme_initial_prompts.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Senior Product Manager | Acme Corp
jordan.lee@acmecorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit follow-up & prompt collection — prompt handling & eval plan

Thanks Jordan — got the CSV. I’ll send the secure upload link for raw prompts in a separate note (we use an expiring S3 share with audit logging). For now: please send a redacted sample with placeholders for ticket IDs and emails, and a 10-row raw sample via the secure share so we can validate redaction impact.

Redaction guidance (short):
- Replace emails with [EMAIL], phone numbers with [PHONE], ticket IDs with [TICKET_ID].
- For code snippets, keep the snippet but replace any secrets/keys with [REDACTED].
- If you can, include both the redacted and one raw sample row per category so we can measure if redaction affects quality.

Eval plan: Marcus will run the following:
- Models: redwood-13b-quant (cost-quality), redwood-3-small (low-latency fallback)
- Metrics: instruction-following accuracy (manually labeled sample), hallucination rate (manual), latency p95, token cost per 1k responses, and basic ROUGE for summary tasks.
- Edge-case checks: Spanish subset, code-snippet handling, very short-context cases.

Marcus — can you kick off the eval once Jordan uploads the secure sample? Target: initial report (metrics + short notes) by Tue 6/30 EOD.

Also linking the current benchmark run for context: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-model-fit-2026

Best,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit follow-up & prompt collection — kicking off evals

On it — will run the two configs on the attached CSV once Jordan completes the secure upload. I’ll produce the following in the initial report:
- Per-category accuracy and hallucination rate (sample size: 200 where possible)
- Latency p50/p95, and cost-per-1k tokens estimates
- A small set of counterexamples where outputs are clearly wrong or unsafe

ETA: I expect first-pass metrics in ~48 hrs after we have the secure sample. If the redacted vs raw comparison is available we’ll include a short note on any material differences.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Program Manager, Model Ops | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit follow-up & prompt collection — timeline

Thanks team — we’ll get the secure upload to you by EOD today. Quick Q on timeline: if the initial report is ready by Tue EOD (6/30), what’s a realistic runway to a small pilot (1k daily requests) if the results look good? Also, do you recommend any quantization/latency tweaks for the production path?

Appreciate it — we’ll share the upload confirmation shortly.

Best,
Jordan
